chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) asked Jibraeel (peace be upon him): 'How was the destruction of the people of Salih (peace be upon him)?' So he said: 'O Muhammad! Salih Salih was sent to his people while he was sixteen years old, so he remained with them until he reached the age of one hundred and twenty years, but they did not respond to him for good.'

And they had seventy idols which they worshipped apart from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So when he saw that from them, he said: 'O people! I was sent to you while I was sixteen years old, and I have now reached one hundred and twenty years, and I present to you two matters. If you wish, ask me until I ask my God, and He will answer you with what you asked me of immediately. And if you wish, I will ask your gods, and if they answer me with what I ask them of, I will leave you, for I have become weary of you and you of me.' They said: 'You have been fair, O Salih.'

So they prepared for a day on which they would go out. He said: So they went out with their idols upon their backs, then they brought forward their food and drink, so they ate and drank. And when they finished, they called him and said: 'O Salih, ask!' So he said to their elder: 'What is the name of this one?' They said: 'Such and such.' So Salih said to it: 'O Such and such, answer!' But it did not answer him. So Salih said: 'What is wrong with it that it does not answer?' They said: 'Call another one.' So he called all of them by their names, but nothing from them answered him. So they turned to their idols and said to them: 'What is wrong with you that you do not answer Salih?' But they did not answer. So they said: 'Step aside from us and leave us and our gods for a while.'

Then they moved aside their rugs and furnishings, and moved aside their clothes, and wallowed upon the dust, and threw dust upon their heads, and said to their idols: 'If you do not answer Salih today, you will be exposed.' He said: Then they called him and said: 'O Salih, call to them.' So he called to them, but they did not answer him. So he said to them: 'O people! The forenoon has passed, and I do not see your gods answering me. So ask me until I call to my God, and He will answer you immediately.'

So seventy men from their elders and the prominent ones among them were delegated to him, and they said: 'O Salih, we ask you. If your Lord answers you, we will follow you and answer to you, and all the people of our town will pledge allegiance to you.' So Salih (peace be upon him) said to them: 'Ask me whatever you wish.' They said: 'Lead us to this mountain,' and the mountain was near to them. So Salih went with them.

When they reached the mountain, they said: 'O Salih, call to your Lord for us, that He may bring out for us from this mountain immediately a she-camel, red, blonde, tame, with a mile between its sides.'

So Salih said to them: 'You have asked me for something that is great for me, but is easy for my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.' He said: So Salih asked Allah, the High, for that, and the mountain split with a split that their intellects nearly flew away when they heard that sound.

Then that mountain trembled with a severe tremble like a woman when labor takes her. Then they were not surprised except that its head had appeared to them from that split. And its neck was not completed until it chewed its cud, then the rest of its body came out, then it stood upright on the ground.

So when they saw that, they said: 'O Salih, how quickly your Lord answered you! Call to your Lord for us that He may bring out for us its young.' So he asked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for that, and she threw it out, and it walked around her.

So he said to them: 'O people, is there anything left?' They said: 'No. Go with us to our people, we will inform them of what we have seen, and they will believe in you.' He said: So they returned, and the seventy had not reached them until sixty-four men had reneged, and they said: 'It is sorcery and a lie.'

They said: So they arrived to all of them, and the six said: 'It is truth,' and all the others said: 'It is a lie and sorcery.' He said: So they turned away upon that, then one of the six was overcome by doubt, and he was the one who slaughtered it.

Ibn Mahboub said: So I narrated this hadith to a man from our companions called Saeed ibn Yazeed, and he informed me that he had seen the mountain from which it came out in Syria. He said: I saw its side, the mountain had scratched it, and its side had left an impression in it, and between it and this other mountain was a mile.
ai.seo_question: What was the sign of the she-camel given to the people of Salih and how did they react?
ai.summary: This detailed narrative from Al-Kafi highlights the theological test of divine power versus idolatry, where Prophet Salih (AS) challenges the leaders to summon their gods, exposing their impotence before producing the she-camel from the rock. The story underscores the Shia emphasis on the miraculous signs (Ayat) and the eventual punishment of those who reject the truth despite clear evidence, specifically noting the betrayal of the seventy delegates and the death of the camel. It also connects to the physical reality of the miracle, as cited by scholars, with the mark of the camel remaining on the mountain in Syria.
